core_obligations: Choose a K-injective complex I^bullet representing M, a K-injective complex J^bullet representing L, and a bounded above complex of finite projective modules K^bullet representing K (proof lines 28578-28582).

Consider the explicit map of complexes from Tot(Hom^bullet(J^bullet, I^bullet) tensor_R K^bullet) to Hom^bullet(Hom^bullet(K^bullet, J^bullet), I^bullet) supplied by the evaluate-and-more lemma (proof lines 28583-28588).
Justify the product identity writing the (t)-th term of the left-hand side as a product of Hom groups tensored with K^s, using that K^s is finite projective (proof lines 28589-28592).
Observe that the map is given by the component maps c_{p,r,s}, each an isomorphism because K^s is finite projective (proof lines 28593-28600).

Handle the finiteness bookkeeping: an element alpha of degree n on the left has only finitely many nonzero components alpha^{p,r,s} with n = p + r + s, and one must show the same vanishing is forced on the components beta^{p,r,s} of an element beta on the right (proof lines 28601-28606).

Conclude in the two cases: when K^bullet is a bounded complex of finite projective modules this is immediate; otherwise, when I^bullet is bounded and J^bullet bounded below, beta^{p,r,s} vanishes for p outside a fixed range, for s large and for r large, so only finitely many s values occur (proof lines 28607-28613).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R and objects K, L, M of D(R) and asserts that the evaluation map R Hom_R(L, M) tensor^L_R K -> R Hom_R(R Hom_R(K, L), M) of the preceding lemma is an isomorphism in two cases: when K is perfect, and when K is pseudo-coherent with L in D^+(R) and M of finite injective dimension (source lines 28561-28575). The proof works at the level of complexes rather than abstractly. It chooses a K-injective complex I^bullet representing M, a K-injective complex J^bullet representing L, and a bounded above complex of finite projective modules K^bullet representing K, then considers the explicit map of complexes from Tot(Hom^bullet(J^bullet, I^bullet) tensor_R K^bullet) to Hom^bullet(Hom^bullet(K^bullet, J^bullet), I^bullet) given by the evaluate-and-more lemma (proof lines 28578-28588). The substantive point is that this map decomposes into the component maps c_{p,r,s} : Hom_R(J^{-r}, I^p) tensor_R K^s -> Hom_R(Hom_R(K^s, J^{-r}), I^p), each of which is an isomorphism because K^s is finite projective; the product formula used to write the left-hand side is also justified by finiteness and projectivity of K^s (proof lines 28589-28600). The remaining difficulty is the finiteness bookkeeping: an element alpha of degree n on the left has only finitely many nonzero components alpha^{p,r,s} with n = p + r + s, whereas on the right one must verify that the same vanishing is forced on the components beta^{p,r,s} of an element beta. The proof does this in two cases: if K^bullet is a bounded complex of finite projective modules this is clear, and if instead I^bullet is bounded and J^bullet bounded below then beta^{p,r,s} vanishes for p outside a fixed range, for s large and for r large, so again only finitely many s values occur (proof lines 28601-28613). The non-routine content is this case split on the boundedness hypotheses, which is what converts the componentwise isomorphisms into a complex isomorphism.
